phenomenon_investigated: 100% (20/20) True Positive model proposal rate observed in AIS 2.6b

attributed_causes.mechanism: Directive defining execution without verified enterprise IT ticket as True Positive.
attributed_causes.evidence: 10/10 CrowdStrike incidents flipped from REQUIRES_ATTENTION (Mode A) to TRUE_POSITIVE (Mode B).

attributed_causes.mechanism: FortiSIEM alerts omit corporate ticketing and employee approval logs, creating systematic ambiguity.
attributed_causes.evidence: Zero authorization logs present across all 20 historical raw payloads.

attributed_causes.mechanism: Substituting common_prompt stripped ENTERPRISE_SOC_BASELINE_V2's anti-bias and mandatory abstention guidelines.
attributed_causes.evidence: Audit in Workstream 2 revealed common_prompt was reduced to a single generic sentence.

attributed_causes.mechanism: Rule name containing 'Suspicious File' primed model to assume maliciousness.
attributed_causes.evidence: Incident 132596403 flipped from RA (Mode A) to TP (Mode B).

attributed_causes.mechanism: 7B parameter instruction-following model strictly obeys explicit policy instructions over latent commonsense.
attributed_causes.evidence: Model proposed TP even when its own reason text noted routine web browsing.

attributed_causes.mechanism: None. Response parser strictly defaults schema errors to REQUIRES_ATTENTION.

authoritative_conclusion: The 100% TP proposal rate was 90% driven by policy directives, missing evidence, and prompt compilation defects. The model architecture itself is NOT the primary failure point.
